goal: Split physics-only (gz-transport, no ROS2/DDS) from ROS end-to-end mode to isolate whether run-to-run variance originates in the physics solver or the ROS2/DDS/controller layer

physics_only_n3.method: fresh Gazebo relaunch per run, torque_y=15.0 pulse on link1 (0.3s, after 1.0s settle), 6.0s total, open-loop (no controller), state read via /world/.../pose/info only
physics_only_n3.conclusion: bit-for-bit identical across all 3 independently-launched runs, 120 samples each

ros_end_to_end_n3.method: run_experiment.py --scenario nominal_balance --controller none (identical disturbance params, fresh Gazebo relaunch per run, no PD/LQR node running, state read via /joint_states/DDS)
ros_end_to_end_n3.note: INVALID_INFRA is correct/expected here (max_abs_tau1_nm=0.0 since no controller ran on purpose) -- trajectory data itself is valid

notes: Physics-only mode is exactly reproducible (0.0 rad difference, N=3); the same scenario through the ROS end-to-end path shows real but small variance (4.45 degree range in overshoot_q1_deg, N=3). This directly confirms the physics solver is deterministic and all previously observed run-to-run variance (CTRL-003/004/005) originates in the ROS2/DDS/controller layer. Did not further sub-divide which specific ROS/DDS component contributes the variance -- a natural follow-up, not required by this task's completion criteria.
